questions.question: Datasets A (56, 58, 60, 62, 64) and B (30, 45, 60, 75, 90) both have mean 60. Their ranges are:
options: A: 8 and B: 60 — same centre, very different spread
both 60, since the means match
A: 60 and B: 8
A: 64 and B: 90

questions.question: Every serious data report carries two kinds of number because:
options: one number is never enough for full marks
a centre says where the data sits, and a spread says how far it wanders — two datasets can share a centre yet tell opposite stories
the range must always be double-checked
means and medians usually disagree

questions.question: The range's weakness is that:
options: it requires the data to be ordered
it cannot be computed for test scores
it uses only the two most extreme values, so one outlier owns it completely — a 95 joining dataset A blows the range from 8 to 39
it is always larger than the IQR

questions.question: For the ordered sales 3, 5, 8, 10, 12, 13, 18, 21, 24, 26, 33 the median is:
options: 12, the fifth value
the sixth value, 13 — five below and five above
18, the middle of the page

questions.question: The lower and upper quartiles of the dataset are:
The interquartile range is:
options: Q3 − Q1 = 24 − 8 = 16 — the width of the middle half of the days

questions.question: The IQR is called the outlier-resistant range because:
options: it is smaller than the range
outliers are deleted before computing it
the extreme days (3 and 33) sit outside the quartile fences, so they cannot stretch it
it uses the mean instead of the median

subtopics.title: The Five-Number Summary and the Box-and-Whisker Diagram

questions.question: The five-number summary of the juice data is:
options: 3, 8, 13, 24, 33 — minimum, Q1, median, Q3, maximum

questions.question: In the box-and-whisker diagram, the box itself:
options: runs from the minimum to the maximum
runs from Q1 at 8 to Q3 at 24 — its length IS the IQR, and it holds the middle half of the data
is centred on the mean
holds all the data except the median

questions.question: Each of the four sections of any box plot contains:
options: a number of days proportional to its length
the values closest to the mean
one quarter of the data — always, no matter how long the section looks
at most one data value

questions.question: The left whisker spans 3 to 8 while the right whisker spans 24 to 33. This means:
options: the right whisker holds more days
the left whisker holds more days
the diagram is drawn incorrectly
both hold a quarter of the days — the quiet quarter is tightly bunched, the busy quarter is spread out

subtopics.title: Percentiles, Skew and Comparing Two Box Plots

questions.question: 'The 75th percentile of sales was 24' is the same statement as:
options: 'Q3 was 24'
'the median was 24'
'the maximum was 24'
'75 percent of days sold exactly 24 cups'

questions.question: A selection squad taking only learners at the 90th percentile demands:
options: a mark of at least 90 percent on the paper
a mark that only 10 percent of candidates beat — percentiles rank you against the group, not the paper
any distinction-level mark
the top 90 percent of candidates

questions.question: The juice data's median sits 5 units from Q1 but 11 from Q3, with a longer right whisker. The distribution is:
options: symmetrical
skewed to the left
skewed to the right — most days bunch low with a tail of big sales days
bimodal

questions.question: Class A: median 62, IQR 10. Class B: median 58, IQR 26. The full two-sentence comparison is:
options: A scored higher; nothing else can be said
B is better because its box is longer
the two classes are identical
A typically scored higher (62 vs 58) AND was more consistent (IQR 10 vs 26)

questions.question: Both pizza places average 40 minutes, but their ranges are 4 and 30 minutes. The flyer's average hides:
options: how far deliveries wander from the centre — the reliability of the service
the price of the pizzas
which place is closer to your house
the number of deliveries per night

questions.question: Spread is described as 'the wandering' because:
options: data points physically move
it measures how far values stray from the centre, which the average cannot show
ranges are calculated while walking
only outliers wander

questions.question: One freak delivery — a flat tyre — balloons the range even if every other pizza was on time. This shows:
options: the range should be doubled for safety
flat tyres must be excluded from data
averages are more reliable than ranges
the range hears only the two most extreme stories, never the everyday ones

subtopics.title: Folding the Line in Half, Then in Half Again

questions.question: Folding the strip of eleven ordered numbers at its middle lands on:
options: the sixth number, 13 — the median, with five numbers on each side
the fifth number, 12
the crease between 12 and 13
whichever number is largest

questions.question: The second and third folds — middles of each half — land on:
options: 5 and 26
8 and 24: the lower and upper quartiles
10 and 21
3 and 33

questions.question: The width between the two outer creases — 8 to 24 — measures:
options: the full range of the data
the number of ordinary days
how wide 'ordinary' is: the IQR of 16, which the wild days at 3 and 33 cannot stretch
the semi-interquartile range

questions.question: Narrating the box plot from the summary 3, 8, 13, 24, 33: the walls of the box rise at:
options: 3 and 33
13 and 24
3 and 13
8 and 24, with the median line inside at 13

questions.question: 'Long never means many; long means spread' warns that:
options: a long section holds the same quarter of the data as a short one — just stretched over more values
longer boxes contain more data
whiskers should be kept short
the number line must not be too long

questions.question: Comparing two boxes on one number line always takes two sentences:
options: one about colours, one about labels
one comparing medians (centre), one comparing box lengths (spread and consistency)
one about the minimum, one about the maximum
one per whisker
